memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The servant hurried to meet her and said, 'Please give me a little water from your jar.' 'Drink, my lord,' she said, and quickly lowered the jar to her hands and gave him a drink. After she had given him a drink, she said, 'I'll draw water for your camels too, until they have had enough to drink.' So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to draw more water, and drew enough for all his camels. Without saying a word, the man watched her closely to learn whether or not the LORD had made his journey successful." - Gen 24:17-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rebekah gives more than she is asked. The servant requests only a little water; she offers to water all ten camels until they finish. A thirsty camel can drink a great deal, so this was heavy, sweaty work she took on for a total stranger. Nobody was watching to reward her. She simply had a generous, serving heart.

Notice the small words: "quickly," "ran." She serves with energy and joy, not grudgingly. This is the kind of person God had prepared — someone whose everyday kindness revealed her character.

Our true character shows most when no one important is watching and when there is nothing to gain. Rebekah did not know a life-changing proposal was moments away. She was simply being herself.

Jesus taught that the one who goes the second mile reflects the heart of the kingdom (Matt 5:41). Today, someone may ask you for a little. Consider giving more than expected. Small, quiet acts of service are never wasted — God sees them, and He often uses them in ways we never imagine.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I serve quickly and cheerfully, or grudgingly?
2. Where can I offer more than what is asked today?
3. Is my character the same when no one is watching?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a generous heart like Rebekah's, ready to serve beyond what is asked. Let my kindness be genuine even when no one notices. Amen.
